title: runtime/lua/vim/_watch.lua:99: ENOENT: no such file or directory
body:
### Problem

Set up lsp per instructions, open an Go file in a Go project on neovim HEAD, I see error message:

```
LSP[gopls]: Error SERVER_REQUEST_HANDLER_ERROR: "...eovim/HEAD-0c0be09/share/nvim/runtime/lua/vim/_watch.lua:100: ENOENT: no such file or directory"
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. install gopls: `go install golang.org/x/tools/gopls@latest`
    ```
    $ gopls version
    golang.org/x/tools/gopls v0.15.2
    ```
2. run the following:
    - `mkdir -p ~/tmp/test-nvim`
    - `cd ~/tmp/test-nvim`
    - `go mod init test-nvim`
    - `go work init`
3. create `test.lua` with content:
    ```lua
    vim.lsp.start({
	    name = "gopls",
	    cmd = { "gopls" },
	    root_dir = vim.fs.dirname(vim.fs.find({ "go.work", "go.mod" }, { upward = true })[1]),
    })
    ```
4. `nvim --clean -u ~/tmp/test-nvim/test.lua main.go`
5. Error shows:

```
LSP[gopls]: Error SERVER_REQUEST_HANDLER_ERROR: "...eovim/HEAD-0c0be09/share/nvim/runtime/lua/vim/_watch.lua:99: ENOENT: no such fil
e or directory"
```

I put a debug print statement in https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/master/runtime/lua/vim/_watch.lua#L99

```lua
  print(vim.inspect(path))
```

I see the following message:

```
11:09:45 msg_show "/Users/<user>/tmp/test-nvim"
11:09:45 msg_show "/Users/<user>/tmp/test-nvim/vendor"
11:09:45 msg_show LSP[gopls]: Error SERVER_REQUEST_HANDLER_ERROR: "...eovim/HEAD-0c0be09/share/nvim/runtime/lua/vim/_watch.lua:100: ENOENT: no such file or directory"
```

I believe the lsp handler is trying to add the folders to the file watch list but my project isn't using Go's 'vendor/' directory, it should skip or fail silently. But it shows the error instead.

This error only starts to show up recently. The LSP related functionality is not affected.

**Note** that this doesn't happen with 0.9.5. Tested with:

`/opt/homebrew/Cellar/neovim/0.9.5/bin/nvim --clean -u ~/tmp/test-nvim/test.lua main.go`

### Expected behavior

No error showing

### Neovim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.10.0-dev-2702+g 0c0be09ea Homebrew

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

N/A

### Operating system/version

macOS 14.2.1

### Terminal name/version

kitty 0.33.1

### $TERM environment variable

xterm-kitty

### Installation

homebrew

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
> This would be useful if you provided precise reproduction steps.

@participant8 , mentioned in the comment and I've been able to confirm the difference locally, but this issue is only happening within a Go workspace (where the `go.work` file is located in the file tree).  The LSP error does not occur when opening a project in a module not under a workspace.

Here are the steps to create a small workspace environment to test the issue
```sh
> mkdir workspace
> cd workspace
> mkdir newProject
> cd newProject
> go mod init newProject
> cd ..
> go work init
> go work use ./newProject
> cd newProject
> touch main.go
> nvim main.go
```

Following this flow, I was able to produce the error.  In contrast, a non-workspace module does not produce the issue:

Make sure not to run this under the `workspace` folder from above.
```sh
> mkdir newProject
> cd newProject
> go mod init newProject
> touch main.go
> nvim main.go
```
No error is produced on this flow.

Hope that helps!

Have you installed `fswatch` in your debian12? Neovim using `watch.watchdirs` for linux if `fswatch` not found, using `watch.watch` for MacOS and windows.

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/cd48b72b60af0a8b5a7770ab599e4062e974183d/runtime/lua/vim/lsp/_watchfiles.lua#L10-L16

The `watch.watchdirs` implementation ignored the `ENOENT: no such file or directory` error.
https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/cd48b72b60af0a8b5a7770ab599e4062e974183d/runtime/lua/vim/_watch.lua#L194-L196

That `watch.watch` implementation doesnt.
https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/cd48b72b60af0a8b5a7770ab599e4062e974183d/runtime/lua/vim/_watch.lua#L70-L99

I don't know much about the LSP protocol and `ms.client_registerCapability`(that doesn't used with neovim 0.9.5 during my debugging, i dont know why), the `ENOENT: no such file or directory` error always caused by a subdir of workspace, in my opinion, this can be ignored too in `watch.watch` like `watch.watchdirs`.

comments.author: participant10
comments.body:
This is the final comment I'm gonna make on this issue, but I'm just gonna say this:

Honestly, if this bug was known about beforehand (whether from CI tests, or this issue, etc.) a month+ in-advance, it shouldn't have ever made it into a stable major release (nvim 0.10 stable). Perhaps hiding/censoring comments on this one was not the best idea.

For me, it was happening every single time I edited a new buffer that was configured to use the standard LSP no matter the language/project (which makes sense since it is apart of the default capabilities passed to every lsp server: [see here](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/e20c5fba2c77b7e7ea93363abc987d913e5f9f58/runtime/lua/vim/lsp/protocol.lua#L635)). So what I did is I finally just went in and removed the `didChangeWatchedFiles` capability from the defaults entirely, although it seems to be the underlying libuv file-watcher impl (or, how it's being used/called in nvim, although I doubt that's the issue given the simplicity of the `luv` interface) that is ultimately broken for some reason (and fwiw I'm on macOS not Linux).

Here's the quick & simple solution I came up with if anyone wants to try it (e.g. just put this into your lua vimrc or otherwise `require` and run it during neovim startup):

```lua
-- General/Global LSP Configuration
local api = vim.api
local lsp = vim.lsp

local make_client_capabilities = lsp.protocol.make_client_capabilities
function lsp.protocol.make_client_capabilities()
    local caps = make_client_capabilities()
    if not (caps.workspace or {}).didChangeWatchedFiles then
        vim.notify(
            'lsp capability didChangeWatchedFiles is already disabled',
            vim.log.levels.WARN
        )
    else
        caps.workspace.didChangeWatchedFiles = nil
    end

    return caps
end
```

Personally I don't even understand the point of using a file watcher in neovim when there's already autocmds, `:<nick>`, and `'autoread'`? Which would seem to me to already be capable of handling most cases.

---

**Edit:** some are pointing out that https://github.com/participant13/neovim/commit/533ce576d67463f658c73eb2a9ebc27bcf4d22d4 is resolving some of their errors, but generally this kind of fix would only work if `path` was invalid here? Why would it be invalid?

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/2c88cfcac42d0a4e0b1a1396539b5add807c336c/runtime/lua/vim/_watch.lua#L99

comments.author: participant19
comments.body:
Can fix in lspconfig like this:
return {
  {
    "neovim/nvim-lspconfig",

    -- Fix https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/28058
    init = function()
      local make_client_capabilities = vim.lsp.protocol.make_client_capabilities
      function vim.lsp.protocol.make_client_capabilities()
        local caps = make_client_capabilities()
        if caps.workspace then
          caps.workspace.didChangeWatchedFiles = nil
        end
        return caps
      end
    end,

    ---@participant23 PluginLspOpts
    opts = function(_, opts)
    ...
